name: Onion
soilType: Well-drained fertile sandy loam or alluvial soil with pH 6.5 - 7.5
growthTips: Frequent light irrigations are preferred over heavy flooding.
Stop irrigation 15 days before harvesting and allow tops to fall naturally.

commonDiseases.name: Purple Blotch of Onion
Alternaria porri
High
name: Small water-soaked sunken lesions turning purple in center
Leaves turn yellow and collapse from lesion site
Neck rot of bulbs in storage
Warm humid weather (25-30°C) with persistent dew
Spray NSKE 5% + Cow urine 5% every 10 days
Apply Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L water
Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 1 mL/L water
Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 mL/L water
Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L
Use disease-free sets / seedlings
Ensure wide spacing
Cure bulbs thoroughly in shade before storage
Mango
soilType: Deep, well-drained rich alluvial or red loamy soil (pH 5.5 - 7.5)
growthTips: Stop irrigation 2 months prior to flowering to induce healthy flower bud differentiation.
Prune dead and criss-cross branches after post-harvest in July-August.

commonDiseases.name: Powdery Mildew & Anthracnose
Oidium mangiferae / Colletotrichum gloeosporioides
High
name: White powdery fungal growth covering floral panicles
Blossoms turn brown, dry up, and drop
Black tear-stain lesions on fruits
Cool nights with warm humid days during flowering stage
Spray Wettable Sulfur 80% WP @ 3g/L before flower opening
Apply neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2 mL/L
Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 1.5 mL/L water
Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 mL/L water
Prune tree canopy to maximize direct sunlight
First spray when flower panicles are 3-5 inches long
Banana
soilType: Deep, fertile, well-drained clay loam with high organic matter
growthTips: De-suckering keeps mother plant vigorous and bunches heavy.
Propping with double bamboo poles protects bunches from storm lodging.

commonDiseases.name: Sigatoka Leaf Spot
Mycosphaerella musicola
High
name: Small yellowish spindle streaks parallel to leaf veins
Dark brown elliptical spots with grey centers
Premature leaf collapse reducing bunch weight
High humidity, warm temperature, and water stagnation
De-leafing and burying infected leaves outside plantation
Spray mineral oil 1% emulsion + Trichoderma viride
Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 mL/L + mineral oil 10 mL/L water
Tebuconazole 50% WG @ 0.5 g/L water
Maintain wide spacing for cross ventilation
Ensure deep drainage ditches around plantation
